slug: cultural_spotlight
title: Cultural Spotlight
blurb: Ryanne Deer's Channel 14 News crew expects a tidy cultural spotlight on Domoleáin, but ends up following Bonacco McGulch and the Sanverde St. Firm through sport, pubs and brawls.
authors: Eve
season: T&L
format: prose
---

A small ship jumps into orbit of a beautiful oceanic planet. “Vioxx’s Truth,” captained by a young elf named Ryanne Deer, is here for a simple cultural spotlight on a recently assimilated planet. Erick Volta, the ship's maintenance man, is making preparations for the footage to upload to the computer, linking the storage drives to MCK-425, their robotic cameraman. “[Make sure you hold the camera steady this time, Mick]{Erick Volta}” Erick sarcastically remarks. “[The footage you got of Poppy decapitating the llamanian pirate wasn’t up to the station’s standards.]{Erick Volta}” Speaking of Poppy, she was currently having some lead slugs pulled out of her chest by the crew's doctor, David Hartnell. He carefully plucks the bullets out of the Floran’s chest and sews her back up. David is many things, short, green, a bit stuck up, but you cannot deny his surgical abilities. Ryanne grabbed her equipment and yelled out to her crew, “[Touchdown in 15. This should be a simple cultural spotlight. I don’t want any interplanetary incidents again like last time.]{Ryanne Deer}” With her word, the crew quickly readies itself for filming as the ship lands on a standardized launch pad. Erick double-checks camera feeds as Mick begins filming. Poppy, now sewn and bandaged up, equips her standard armaments. The elven woman turns to the camera with her microphone in hand, making sure she looks nice for the viewers. “[This is Ryanne Deer with Channel 14 News, I’m on Domoleáin, in the binary star system of Janus-55. I’m here to shine a cultural spotlight on this planet’s inhabitants.]{Ryanne Deer}”

Bonacco McGulch rolls off the futon in his run-down apartment, beer cans and wrappers from cheap fast food litter the floor and bed, forming a nest for the faróin. Bonacco pulls himself up onto his feet, nursing yet another hangover. Long days at the factory mean you have to unwind in any way possible, and for McGulch that was booze, drugs, violence, and sports all mixed together. McGulch managed to get the next two weeks off for the peiluisce world tournament, so he and his firm could go on a little tour, smashing skulls, drinking at pubs, and watching the game. McGulch slides his clothes over his nude body, the only outfit for such an occasion, a simple sports jersey and some shorts. McGulch dips his flippers into the facepaint he bought with the little money he had and rubs it on his face, covering his snout and whiskers with blue and red paint. His preparation was interrupted by a knock at the door, expecting it to be a neighbor or a bill collector, he grabbed a nearby baseball bat. Opening the door, he wasn’t greeted by either of those, he opened the door to see an elf in a business suit and a fair bit of makeup. “[Aye who the fuck are yeh?]{Bonacco McGulch}” McGulch slurs out to the group outside of his door, “[I could take on all five of yahs if you are gonna try anythin funny.]{Bonacco McGulch}” Ryanne cleared her throat and responded in a professional tone, “[My name is Ryanne Deer, I'm here for Channel 14 News. We’re here to follow you for a few days and record you.]{Ryanne Deer}” McGulch took a second to remember, he did sign some documents a few weeks ago to get enough money for the world tournament. “[What’s all this for again?]{Bonacco McGulch}” McGulch questioned. “[This is going to be broadcast all across the Galactic Union to show your planet’s culture]{Ryanne Deer},” Ryanne answered. The Sealman cocked a grin; this is his chance to get the Sanverde St. Firm in the public eye. “[Follow me then, gotta get me mates together for the game day.]{Bonacco McGulch}” McGulch pushed the crew aside and ran outside.

“[Ryanne, are you sure these bozos are good for any footage, the man’s a-]{David Hartnell}” David couldn’t finish before Ryanne shut him down with a simple “[Shut it.]{Ryanne Deer}” “[We’re getting our footage whether you like him or not.]{Ryanne Deer}” David scoffed and crossed his arms, annoyed with the situation he found himself in. McGulch led the camera crew to a rundown pub. “[Here’s where all my mates meet up for drinks, should have all of the crew in there.]{Bonacco McGulch}” McGulch swung open the doors to meet the rest of the Sanverde St. Firm. The four men inside cheer when they see their good friend, McGulch. The entire place stank of cheap booze, cheap cigarettes and cheaper food. McGulch sat down with the rest of the firm and started drinking a pint that they had bought for him. “[Christ, this place smells as bad as the cages those slavers kept the Florans in]{Erick Volta},” Erick remarked. “[So what’s up with the camera crew?]{Velhoteim Sábio}” asked the older, scruffier friend of McGulch. McGulch responded after downing his entire drink, “[Some kinda reporters, followin’ me around to show the galaxy what we do ‘round here.]{Bonacco McGulch}” “[You sure this is a good idea, mate? ‘Ate to see them get offed by some wanker from the rivals]{Velhoteim Sábio},” the gruff old walrus said. McGulch laughed, “[No knobhead’s gonna mess with some GU reporters, and if they do-]{Bonacco McGulch}” McGulch cracked his knuckles. “[They’re gonna be eating their dinners from a straw.]{Bonacco McGulch}” McGulch turns around and beckons the crew over, “[Here’s all of the firm members, make sure you get their good angles.]{Bonacco McGulch}” “[This right here’s Velhoteim Sábio, I just call him Sabby, this old cunt used to be in charge before me.]{Bonacco McGulch}” The walrus takes a puff from his cigarette and waves toward the camera. McGulch points towards a tall, plump Míomór playing with some sort of children’s toy, “[This one’s Atratolo, good kid, absolute unit of a lad. Once he flipped a bus that had some stupid wankers on it.]{Bonacco McGulch}” The whale looks up for a second, confused; the look in his eyes is that of someone who can’t count past six, which, considering the group he’s in, is surprisingly stupid. He grunts before going back to smacking the toy against the table. “[These two are Tocci Endente, and Separtida Dançágua, they’re absolute ragers at parties, these two.]{Bonacco McGulch}” Mick moves the camera over a stoned dolphin, and a very anxious seagull. Tocci is currently breathing heavily, his eyes darting around the room, checking every corner for any danger. He looks like he hasn’t slept since he was born, muttering to himself about nonsense. Separtida is giggling about nothing, his movements slowed. He claps his flipper hands together; he may as well be France in the 1940s with how blitzed he was. “[So, ya ready to watch the best firm do their thing?]{Bonacco McGulch}” McGulch gloats to the camera.

Ryanne wasn’t happy; she wasn’t sure anyone on the crew was, except maybe Mick; Mick was always okay. Getting dragged to watch some sports game surrounded by sweaty and fat middle-aged marine mammals. Ryanne sulked in her seat, “[There’s no way anything good can come from this]{Ryanne Deer},” she thought to herself. She begins to dissociate from the scenario she found herself stuck in, all those years of journalism, all the near-death experiences trying to get the scoop on corporate conspiracies, might as well be nothing. She’s stuck watching a bunch of guys slap a ball in the water arou- A sickening crunch echoed throughout the stadium. Ryanne could hear it over the crowd’s screaming; she looked and saw one of the players with their head bashed in with the ball. The others didn’t stop playing, continuing to maim and beat one another. Okay, this was at least interesting; hopefully the editors could tone down the violence on display. The crowd cheers “PELO! PELO! PELO! PELO!” as a faróin slams a ball, sending it careening into the goal. A babhlte tries to scoop the ball into his mouth to intercept it, but the ball breaks his pelican jaw. The ball gets sent off course by this, a duneilf slaps it with his tail, correcting the course back to the intended target. The ball makes it into the goal, air horns and cheering erupt in the stadium as the crowd goes manic.

The Sanverde St. Firm, and the Channel 15 Crew funnel out of the stadium. McGulch, leading a pub crawl, bursts into song. The rest of the firm sing along with him as they go to a bar, drink until they get kicked out, and then move to the next. On the way from one pub to the next, McGulch stops. On the other end of the street was a rival firm. The air changed; everyone went quiet. The tension was thick enough to cut with a knife. McGulch let out a war cry as he and his team charged the other firm. A sudden explosion of violence as they traded blows. Teeth, blood and spit fly as McGulch and his mates beat the piss out of the other firm. Ryanne gave the side-eye to Poppy, “[You can join in if you want.]{Ryanne Deer}” The Floran charged in to strike fear into the hearts of the enemies of Sanverde Street firm. McGulch’s opponents realized they couldn't win the raging battle, so they decided to turn tail and run. McGulch, beaten and bloodied, produced a can of beer and chugged it in less than 3 seconds. He and his crew relished in their victory, cheering, singing and drinking at the enemies’ crushing defeat.

Ryanne had had enough; she lay on the cold metal floor of the ship staring at the ceiling. This was the end of her career. There’s no way anybody would want this footage. “[How you holdin up, miss?]{Erick Volta}” Erick chimed in. Ryanne tilted her head to stare at him, “[Bad.]{Ryanne Deer}” She overheard “[I told her that this was a stupid idea, but nobody listens to me.]{David Hartnell}” “[Hey, don’t listen to him, Mick liked it.]{Erick Volta}” Mick poked his robotic head into the room, a smiley face displayed on the screen. The comm set in her room started ringing; it was the station. She was so fucked, she knew it, she was a failure. She sat down, bracing herself for the death of her journalism life. “[Miss Deer, we have received your footage.]{Channel 14 Station}” Ryanne gulped, she knew what was next. “[We’re sending you a bonus for the excellent footage.]{Channel 14 Station}” Ryanne was confused, was this a prank? She checked her bank account, and sure enough, it was the truth. The call ends rather abruptly. Ryanne is left to herself and the filled bank account.

She split the money among the crew, and went to her personal computer. She began research for her next big scoop.
